summary: David Bradley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. (Hons) at King's College London (1972–1975) and studied at the University of Cambridge from 1975 to 1979.

David Brainerd Spooner (1879–1925) was an indologist and archaeologist. Educated at Stanford, Tokyo, Sampurnanand, and Harvard (Ph.D. under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Richard Pischel), he held several leadership posts at the Archaeological Survey of India between 1906 and 1919.

David Brick is an Indology scholar who studied under Patrick Olivelle. He served as a professor at Yale University (attested 2012–2018) and sat on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies in 2012.

David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge in 1782. He founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society and served as Provost of Fort William College from circa 1800 to 1807.

David Bubna-Litic is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who completed a PhD at Western Sydney University. In 2000, he was a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney.

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). He held posts at Keble College, Oxford in 2001 and Canterbury Christ Church University in 2010.

David Carpenter (born 1949) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of the History of Religions at Saint Joseph's University around 1988 and as Professor of Neurology at Washington University in St. Louis in 2005.

David Dean Shulman (born 1949) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. After studying at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and earning his doctorate under John Ralston Marr at SOAS/University of London, he held professorial and directorial posts at Hebrew University.

David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Lawrence, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (Ph.D. under Karen Christina Lang), he has held teaching posts at Virginia, Indiana University Bloomington (2006), and the University of Manitoba (2008–2010).

David E. Cooper (born 1942) is a philosopher who studied at St Edmund Hall, Oxford. He lectured at Oxford in 1967, served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and was a visiting professor at Peking University in 2022.

David E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. at UCLA, he taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and held research posts at Nichibunken (2006) and Oberlin College (2010).

David Faure (born 1947) is a historian and sinologist. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and Princeton University (Ph.D.), lectured at St Antony's College, taught at Indiana University Bloomington, and directed at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

David Fiordalis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, Chicago, and Michigan (Ph.D. under Luis Oscar Gómez), he became an associate professor at Linfield University and research editor for 84000.

David Friedman (1903–1984) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. Educated at Utrecht, Oxford, and Leiden (Ph.D.), he taught at Leiden (1938–1940), the University of Indonesia (1946–1950), and SOAS/University of London (1950–1970).

David Gellner (born 1957) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held multiple posts at the University of Oxford from 1988 through 2024, becoming Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology at Wolfson College by 2026.

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After receiving his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992, he joined the University of Virginia as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies that same year.
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education under traditional teachers Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Goodman Mandelbaum (1911–1987) was an Indologist. He earned his B.A. at Northwestern and Ph.D. at Yale under Edward Sapir, later holding academic posts at the University of Minnesota (1938–1946) and UC Berkeley (1946–1978).

David Gordon White (born 1953) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Wisconsin-Madison, BHU, and Chicago (Ph.D.), he held faculty posts at the University of Virginia and UC Santa Barbara, where he became J. F. Rowny Professor.

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a researcher at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
